abstract: We study how redistribution between asset holders and non‐asset holders links macroeconomic fluctuations to expected stock returns. Aggregate and relative consumption growth forecast excess returns with opposite signs and at different horizons. We interpret these patterns using a production‐based asset‐pricing model with limited participation and external habits. Aggregate (relative) consumption captures variation in the price (quantity) of risk. Technology shocks drive macroeconomic fluctuations, whereas redistributive shocks generate large short‐run movements in inequality and are the main source of priced risk. This points to a macro‐finance disconnect between the drivers of business cycles and those governing risk premia.
title: Asset Market Participation, Redistribution, and Asset Pricing

abstract: We propose a nonrecursive VAR identification strategy that separately identifies short‐term and long‐term uncertainty shocks by exploiting sign restrictions implied by a stylized framework and a DSGE model featuring both types of shocks. We find that long‐term uncertainty shocks exert strong and persistent effects on real activity, whereas short‐term shocks have limited real effects. We use the DSGE model to study their differential propagation and show that time‐to‐build is an important ingredient allowing the model to account for the stark empirical asymmetry in investment and, in turn, output—both contract sharply after long‐term shocks but only modestly after short‐term shocks.
title: Real Activity and Uncertainty Shocks: The Long and the Short of It

abstract: I propose a mechanism through which institutional investors’ correlated demand shocks provide a source of market risk in asset pricing. Institutional investors have mandates to beat a similar market index. During periods of strong stock market performance, their incentive to outperform intensifies as more of them fall short of the market index. This incentive induces procyclical risk-taking behavior, generating correlated demand that elevates the market betas and risk premia of exposed stocks. Quasi-experiments using exogenous changes in index membership support a causal interpretation of the mechanism. Elevated betas are associated with a higher perceived cost of capital and reduced firm investment. (JEL G1, G2)
title: Correlated Demand Shocks and Asset Pricing

abstract: When a counter-proposal is made to an initiative to change the Swiss constitution, the citizenry makes three binary majority choices: the initiative versus the status quo, the counter-proposal versus the status quo, and the initiative versus the counter-proposal as a tie-breaker. If the three majority choices form a cycle, the current rule selects the alternative that beats the status quo. This rule may lead to strategic voting. We suggest breaking cycles differently by choosing the middle alternative in case of a cycle, which will normally be the counter-proposal. More precisely, we study Condorcet-consistent pairwise majority voting procedures when preferences are single-peaked and their distribution is common knowledge. We then show that whenever a strong Nash equilibrium exists, its outcome is the same as under sincere voting, and we characterize the cycle-breaking defaults for which sincere voting is itself a strong Nash equilibrium. In particular, among procedures that use the same default for both possible cycles, the middle alternative is the unique common default.
title: A Better Cycle-Breaker for Direct Democracy?

abstract: Decarbonising the hard-to-abate maritime and aviation transport sectors will be challenging. Alternative renewable fuels, such as biofuels and E-fuels, show promising potential for substituting traditional fossil fuels, but carry challenges regarding the expansion of variable renewable energy (VRE) and the availability of sustainable biomass. This study assesses these challenges and regional impacts using a comprehensive sector-coupled energy system modelling framework applied to Europe. Under high biomass availability, a documented substitution effect allows the share of E-kerosene and biokerosene to shift with VRE accessibility, whereas this flexibility declines under biomass scarcity. These differences are reflected in fuel costs: aviation fuel prices are more sensitive to biomass scarcity, while maritime fuel prices are more sensitive to VRE restrictions. Regional resource availability reshapes renewable fuel production and trade. Under the modelling assumptions, accessible VRE resources favour E-fuel supply-chains from Spain, while lower VRE accessibility increases the role of biomass-rich countries, including Germany and Poland, as exporters. Constrained VRE deployment results in increased infrastructure needs, lowers average renewable capacity factors, and raises total system costs by up to 9%. Finally, increasing scarcity increases the importance of carbon management. Biomass is prioritised for fuel production and industrial applications coupled with carbon capture, while direct air capture and carbon reuse become increasingly important for meeting fuel demand. These results highlight the need for coordinated policies on biomass utilisation, VRE deployment, carbon management, and infrastructure planning to achieve cost-efficient decarbonisation of Europe's hard-to-abate transport sectors.
abstract_zh: 难以减排的海运和航空运输部门脱碳将颇具挑战性。生物燃料和电制燃料等替代可再生燃料展现出替代传统化石燃料的潜力，但在可变可再生能源（VRE）扩张和可持续生物质可用性方面面临挑战。本研究采用一个综合的部门耦合能源系统建模框架应用于欧洲，评估这些挑战及区域影响。在生物质高可用性下，一种有文献记载的替代效应使得电制煤油和生物煤油的比例可随VRE可及性变化而转移，而在生物质稀缺下这种灵活性下降。这些差异反映在燃料成本上：航空燃料价格对生物质稀缺更为敏感，而海运燃料价格对VRE限制更为敏感。区域资源可用性重塑可再生燃料生产和贸易。在建模假设下，可及的VRE资源有利于来自西班牙的电制燃料供应链，而较低的VRE可及性则增强了包括德国和波兰在内的生物质丰富国家作为出口国的作用。受限的VRE部署导致基础设施需求增加，降低平均可再生容量系数，并使系统总成本增加高达9%。最后，日益加剧的稀缺性提高了碳管理的重要性。生物质被优先用于燃料生产及与碳捕集相结合的工业应用，而直接空气捕集和碳再利用对于满足燃料需求变得日益重要。这些结果凸显了在生物质利用、VRE部署、碳管理和基础设施规划方面采取协调政策的必要性，以实现欧洲难以减排运输部门的经济高效脱碳。

abstract: Did immigration from Eastern Europe increase Euroscepticism in Britain? This study examines how this migration wave influenced British Euroscepticism. Using longitudinal survey data and an instrumental variable strategy, I provide causal evidence that the inflow of Eastern European migrants led to increased Eurosceptic attitudes. The migration inflow also increased comparative national attachment and perceived crime risk.

abstract: The 20th century shift from sterling to the dollar is often cited as evidence that currency dominance is not forever. This column presents a nonlinear model of the international monetary system calibrated on historical events. Shifts in dominance require large, simultaneous combinations of shocks, with democracy and conflicts playing a central role. Stress tests suggest that dollar dominance is resilient: a decline would require repeated shocks in the US alongside major reforms in China and Europe. Parallels between the dollar’s rise in the 20th century and that of the renminbi in the 21st century should be treated with extreme caution.
abstract_zh: 20世纪从英镑到美元的转变常被引为货币主导地位并非永恒的证据。本专栏提出一个基于历史事件校准的国际货币体系非线性模型。主导地位的转变需要大规模、同时发生的冲击组合，其中民主与冲突发挥核心作用。压力测试表明，美元主导地位具有韧性：其衰落需要美国反复遭受冲击，同时中国和欧洲进行重大改革。应将20世纪美元崛起与21世纪人民币崛起之间的类比极为谨慎地对待。

abstract: International financial integration is often measured through national totals. Yet these totals can conceal very different experiences across firms. Using comprehensive French microdata, this column shows that most financially internationalised firms raise foreign equity without investing abroad, while a small group of large firms dominates cross-border positions. Foreign funding is associated with greater equity financing, lower bank debt, and higher investment. This heterogeneity also means that aggregate estimates understate the importance of country factors for the cross-border allocations of the typical firm.
abstract_zh: 国际金融一体化通常通过国家总量来衡量。然而，这些总量可能掩盖了企业间截然不同的经历。利用全面的法国微观数据，本专栏表明，大多数金融国际化企业筹集外国股权但并未对外投资，而一小部分大型企业主导了跨境头寸。外国融资与更高的股权融资、更低的银行债务和更高的投资相关联。这种异质性也意味着，总量估计低估了国家因素对典型企业跨境配置的重要性。

abstract: This paper develops a two-dimensional crisis typology that classifies the impact of major crisis episodes on return spillover connectedness across energy transition metals (ETM) markets. Using daily data for 17 metals, spanning base metals, precious metals, battery metals, and technology metals, and the rolling-window Diebold–Yılmaz (2012) connectedness framework, the paper classifies 11 crisis events between 2017 and 2025 along two orthogonal axes: the direction of the connectedness shift (integration vs. fragmentation) and the stability of the response (volatile vs. stable), with the latter benchmarked against a bootstrap-derived threshold from pre-crisis markets. The typology reveals a fragmentation paradox: supply-side shocks (armed conflicts and bilateral trade restrictions) consistently decrease market connectedness, while demand-side shocks (pandemics, monetary tightening, and financial crises) consistently increase it. This dichotomy, which is robustly preserved across all 25 event-study window specifications, challenges the prevailing assumption in the connectedness literature that crises uniformly amplify systemic risk through heightened spillovers. The mechanism is grounded in the distinction between common-factor and idiosyncratic transmission channels: supply disruptions affect individual metals asymmetrically based on their geographic exposure, fragmenting the co-movement structure, while demand shocks operate through common macroeconomic channels that drive all metals together. The typology has implications for strategic reserves policy, portfolio hedging, and energy transition risk assessment, suggesting that geopolitical risk to critical minerals supply chains is more modular than the contagion hypothesis predicts.
abstract_zh: 本文构建了一个二维危机类型学，用于分类重大危机事件对能源转型金属（ETM）市场间收益溢出关联性的影响。基于17种金属（涵盖基本金属、贵金属、电池金属和技术金属）的日度数据，并采用滚动窗口Diebold–Yılmaz（2012）关联性框架，本文将2017年至2025年间的11次危机事件沿两条正交轴进行分类：关联性变化的方向（整合与碎片化）和响应的稳定性（波动与稳定），后者以危机前市场通过自助法得出的阈值为基准。该类型学揭示了一个碎片化悖论：供给侧冲击（武装冲突和双边贸易限制）持续降低市场关联性，而需求侧冲击（流行病、货币紧缩和金融危机）持续提高市场关联性。这一二分法在所有25种事件研究窗口设定下均稳健保持，挑战了关联性文献中关于危机通过加剧溢出效应统一放大系统性风险的主流假设。其机制根植于共同因子与特质性传导渠道的区分：供给中断基于各金属的地理暴露对其产生不对称影响，从而碎片化共同运动结构；而需求冲击通过驱动所有金属共同运动的共同宏观经济渠道发挥作用。该类型学对战略储备政策、投资组合对冲和能源转型风险评估具有启示意义，表明关键矿产供应链的地缘政治风险比传染假说所预测的更具模块化特征。
title: Do crises integrate or fragment energy transition metals markets? Evidence from a connectedness-based crisis typology
title_zh: 危机是整合还是分裂能源转型金属市场？——基于连通性危机类型学的证据

abstract: I study spillovers from U.S. bond supply shocks, identified from yield moves around U.S. Treasury auction announcements. Using the shocks as instruments in daily and monthly local projections for AEs and EMs, I find substantial pass-through to global long-term rates. A debt expansion shock that raises the U.S. 10-year yield by 10 bps lifts foreign 10-year yields by roughly 7 bps within a few business days. Monthly aggregation shows contractionary real effects: U.S. industrial production falls up to 0.4 percent after eight months and foreign industrial production by a comparable amount, around 0.4 percent, with a more persistent profile. The foreign contraction reflects financial tightening, exchange-rate depreciation, and weaker U.S. demand. Spillovers are heterogeneous: moving from the 25th to 75th percentile of foreign investor participation deepens the IP decline by 0.5 pp. Results are robust to a demand-side shock and consistent with the relevant benchmarks, highlighting U.S. bond supply as a key driver of global financial conditions and real activity, amplified by foreign investor participation and weak domestic fundamentals.

abstract: This paper estimates the macroeconomic effects of forced displacement on host economies in SubSaharan Africa, drawing on cross-country panel data and country case studies of Burkina Faso, South Sudan, and Uganda to provide granular evidence on the consequences of spatial concentrations of forcibly displaced persons within countries. Estimates from a difference-in-differences local projections (LP-DiD) framework do not suggest that large refugee inflows significantly affect host-country GDP, inflation, or the current account balance over a five-year horizon. The effects on the primary fiscal balance also appear to be muted, yet this masks offsetting fiscal dynamics: government expenditures rise and fiscal revenues increase (mainly through taxes). These results are robust to restricting the control group to Sub-Saharan African economies. Under a broader treatment definition that captures the total displaced population (refugees and internally displaced persons), the GDP response turns significantly negative and intensifies with displacement severity, though this estimate is best interpreted as an upper bound because it cannot be fully separated from the effects of conflict itself that generates displacement. The cross-country findings are consistent with the case studies, which indicate generally muted effects on aggregate food inflation and wages. Beneath this muted aggregate response, however, a consistent pattern emerges across cases: prices of imported and processed staples rise, while those of locally produced cereals stay flat or fall. The case studies also yield mixed evidence regarding the impacts of displacement inflows on consumption and labor force participation, with such inflows reducing host employment in Burkina Faso but raising it in Uganda.
authors: Hany Abdel-Latif & Mr. Antonio David & Mouhamadou Moustapha Ly & Elisee Wendlassida Miningou & Masateru Okamoto & Alex Vaval Pierre-Charles
title: Macroeconomic Effects of Forced Displacement in Sub-Saharan Africa

abstract: The literature characterizes zombie firms as economically unviable companies that continue to operate. This paper proposes that the majority of zombie firms can be viable, with positive continuation value, and arise endogenously from productivity shocks. Drawing on firm-level data covering the universe of Canadian firms and seven European countries, we document five stylized facts: zombie firms are widespread, unprofitable, unproductive, micro-sized, and transitory. We rationalize these findings by building a general equilibrium model of heterogeneous firms that abstracts from the conventional distortions thought to explain zombie firms. We show that standard productivity shocks are sufficient to explain the empirical patterns, and that the volatility of these shocks can be a key determinant of viable zombie firms, generating shares up to 35%. Since this volatility can also raise aggregate productivity and household utility, the presence of zombie firms is not a sufficient condition for lower welfare. Using a model-based definition to distinguish viability, we find limited evidence—around 0.25%—of unviable zombie firms in the data. Our results challenge the prevailing view that persistently weak firms are unviable and suggest that existing zombie firm measures likely capture viable firms.
authors: Alexander Amundsen & Amélie Lafrance-Cooke & Danny Leung
title: Rethinking Zombie Firms: From Volatility to Viability

abstract: This paper analyzes how achieving Europe’s medium-term greenhouse gas mitigation targets enhances energy security, defined as the cushioning of the adverse macroeconomic impact of oil and gas price shocks. It uses the IMF’s Global Macroeconomic Model of the Energy Transition, which combines a rich set of New-Keynesian features with a detailed representation of fossil fuel use, including granular modelling of the transport and heating sectors. Future oil and gas price shocks are simulated in a scenario where Europe’s mitigation policy agenda has been fully implemented (and mitigation targets are met), and in a hypothetical scenario where mitigation policy has remained constant at the current level of ambition. A comparison shows that the policy agenda substantially dampens future shock transmission. The inflationary impact of both shocks is close to 40 percent larger under constant policies than under the mitigation agenda, and for oil shocks, the output decline is about twice as large. These energy security co-benefits materialize gradually as the economy adjusts to the mitigation agenda, and are shown to depend on ETS2, the new emissions trading system covering transportation and buildings. An additional exercise proxies for merit-order electricity pricing. In these simulations, the mitigation agenda further reduces pass-through from gas price shocks to electricity prices, thereby enhancing the macroeconomic stabilizing effects.
title: The EU’s Energy Transition and Fuel Price Shocks

abstract: How are inflation expectations affected by foreign supply shocks? We show that, beyond bilateral exposure, a second network matters: the one linking forecasters to the countries they cover. Using forecasterlevel expectations around conflict episodes—precisely dated supply shocks that raise inflation through trade and energy linkages—we find that expectations are revised upward gradually in the days following a conflict. Within the same country and day, forecasters who cover the conflict country revise by 0.2 to 0.3 percentage points less than those who do not, and the differential roughly triples where bilateral exposure is highest. We rationalize this in a model where a public narrative overstates spillovers in proportion to bilateral exposure, and only forecasters covering the conflict country can discount it. The consensus therefore inherits a bias largest where exposure is high and coverage thin, and a central bank reading it at face value tightens more than fundamentals warrant.
title: Information Networks and Inflation Expectations: Evidence from Professional Forecasters and Conflicts

abstract: Revenue mobilization is a key objective in many IMF-supported programs, yet tax revenue-to-GDP forecasts often fall short of outcomes. This paper analyzes the underlying drivers of these forecast misses by leveraging two novel global datasets on tax policy yields and tax administration capacity. It finds that tax revenue-to-GDP forecast errors are primarily driven by over-optimism in forecasted yields of tax policy measures and tax buoyancy assumptions, as well as macroeconomic forecast errors, particularly for growth and trade openness. Stronger tax administration capacity and well-implemented and high-quality revenue related structural reforms are associated with lower forecast errors. Additional empirical analysis shows that over-optimism in forecasted tax policy yields declines significantly when revenue measures are well-designed, part of large-measure revenue packages, and accompanied by high-quality revenue-related structural reforms. Improving forecast realism requires better-grounded yield estimations and tax buoyancy assumptions, explicit consideration of implementation capacity, and a focus on well-designed revenue-related structural reforms.
authors: Jean-Marc Atsebi & Qiaoe Chen & Nikolay Gueorguiev & Magali Pinat
title: Understanding Over-Optimism in Tax Revenue-to-GDP Forecasts under IMF-supported Programs
